_comment: The half of the status board that cannot be read from the repo. Edited as data; tools/status_board.py renders it. Everything else on the board is fetched or computed.

needs_josh.title: Draw every roof in the benchmark cluster
needs_josh.body: The benchmark is 152 roofs and only 11 are drawn, so it can see a big regression but not a small one. Drawing 40–50 roofs in that one cluster would turn it into dense ground truth where a 2% change is visible immediately.
needs_josh.note: This is a change of habit, not extra work: the same effort spent in one place instead of scattered across the district. python tools/bench.py --make writes the id list.

needs_josh.title: Draw sawtooth and repeated-fold roofs
needs_josh.body: Where the detector fails hardest — it finds a building's long axes and misses every cross-fold. Draw each fold all the way across; a complete line teaches far more than a short one.

needs_josh.title: Press B in the markup tool
needs_josh.body: It draws what the build currently makes of each roof under your lines. Any building id where that looks wrong is directly useful.
needs_josh.note: A reference, not a tracing guide — draw what you see, not what it drew.

open.title: District rebuild on the three fixes
open.body: The drawn-face exemption, the cut-frame correction and the working clipper are committed and measured but not yet in a district build. About 4½ hours on the VM, then the deploy gate.
open.note: The live site still carries the old behaviour on unlabelled roofs.

open.title: Six roofs still not reproduced exactly
open.body: After the drawn-face fix, 419 of 438 faces match your markup exactly. The remainder cluster on six roofs — worst is #4732152 at 4 of 7 faces — so there is a second, smaller cause still to find.

open.title: Retrain the detector on the newer labels
open.body: The line model dates from 2 Sep and has not seen the labels added since. The training split now pins a roof's side by its own id, so adding labels no longer reshuffles what the model has already seen.
open.note: Pin the benchmark out of training first: export_training_data.py --val-ids data/bench_ids.txt

open.title: Island Bay is unaffected
open.body: No labelled roofs there and the line model has never run over Wellington's imagery, so every fix here is inert until predict_roof_lines.py is run for it.

rejected.why: Makes the full-width cut problem worse
Under-segments; runs straight over folds you drew
Helps where the roof is, not where it folds
Region targets do not dodge the hard part

rejected.what: Extent clipping without the frame fix
rejected.why: Rejects 163 of 242 cuts by measuring against a chord in the wrong place

constraints: The LiDAR cannot find roof creases. The survey is 1.7 returns/m² — about 0.77 m spacing — and the 1 m DSM is already at native resolution, so a hip crease falls between samples. Imagery must find the lines and LiDAR fit the angles.

The detector emits stubs, not folds. Where you draw a 5 m fold it finds 1.5 m; 98.5% of its line endpoints dangle against 56.4% of yours. More labelled roofs measurably help: boundary F1 has gone 0.122 → 0.185 as labels grew 18 → 74, about +1.1 per 100 roofs, still climbing.
